summary: Settlement postings stopped because order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0, 07:40:00Z) renamed the OrderExecuted field qty->quantity and bumped the event schema to v2, while settlement-service still expects schema v1. Every OrderExecuted event now fails deserialization ('schema v1 expected, header says v2'), the consumer recycles the same offset as a poison message and blocks the partition, so throughput collapses to ~0.4 req/s, settlements post zero, and consumer lag grows from ~47 to 61.6k. The reported consumer poll config change (cfg-3004, 07:35:37) is a red herring: it only shrank batch size and predates the error onset. Kafka is healthy and settlement-service had no deployment and zero restarts. The fault originates in the order-service release; confidence 0.9. Fix: roll back dep-6010 or ship a v2-compatible deserializer in settlement-service, then reset the poisoned consumer offset (or DLQ the stuck message) to unblock the partition.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2 OrderExecuted schema change breaks settlement-service consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0) renamed OrderExecuted field 'qty'->'quantity' and bumped the schema header to v2. settlement-service still deserializes as schema v1, so every OrderExecuted event fails to deserialize; the consumer retries the same offset as a poison message, the partition is blocked, zero settlements post, and consumer lag grows unboundedly. The fault ORIGINATES in the order-service release (contract-breaking producer change), not in settlement-service.

causal_chain.claim: dep-6010 deploys and renames qty->quantity, bumping event schema to v2
settlement-service (schema v1) fails to deserialize OrderExecuted
consumer enters poison-message retry loop and blocks the partition offset
consumption stops (request_rate ~0) so settlements process zero
retry loop drives CPU from ~28% to ~70%

assumptions: settlement-service has no v2 deserializer; the consumer is the only OrderExecuted consumer affected.
All settlement-service partitions fail equally (logs sample partition orders-3).

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service config change (consumer.max.poll.records) caused the stall
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-3004 reduced consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200 at 07:35, starving the consumer and causing lag to grow.
assumptions: Poll batch size alone can reduce throughput to zero.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The change only shrinks poll batch size (500->200) and was applied at 07:35:37, before the 07:42:14 first error; it cannot produce a schema-v1-vs-v2 deserialization failure. Throughput fell to ~0.4 req/s due to deserialize failures, not batch sizing.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka partition reassignment / broker rebalance stalled the consumer (cf. HIST-112)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A Kafka reassignment stranded settlement-service's consumer group, matching historical incident HIST-112.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Kafka logs are clean (only two benign connection resets), restarts=0, and the settled failure mode is an explicit schema-version deserialize error with a poison-message loop, not a lost assignment.

facts.statement: order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0) at 07:40:00Z renamed OrderExecuted qty->quantity and bumped schema to v2.
settlement-service fails to deserialize OrderExecuted: 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)', first at 07:42:14Z.
settlement-service re-enters a poison-message retry loop ('partition blocked') on the same offset.
settlement-service consumer_lag grew from ~47 to 61,605 messages.
settlement-service request_rate collapsed from ~62 to 0.4 req/s, i.e. settlements stopped processing.
settlement-service CPU spiked from ~28% to ~70% consistent with the retry loop.
The config change cfg-3004 (max.poll.records 500->200) was applied at 07:35:37Z, before the first error.
There were zero settlement-service deployments and zero restarts in the window.
Kafka logs and settlement-service db_pool were normal, ruling out broker failure and DB exhaustion.
settlement-service HTTP error_rate stayed flat ~0.2%, so the failure is in the consumer path.

assumptions: settlement-service has no v2 deserializer and is the sole consumer of OrderExecuted.
The lag growth (~5000 msgs per 12 min) reflects unprocessed backlog, consistent with a single consumer group on the orders topic.
dep-6010 is still live (status 'live', not rolled back).

timeline.event: order-service deploy dep-6010 (v2.16.0) with OrderExecuted qty->quantity and schema v2
order-service rollout complete, all pods ready
First settlement-service deserialize error: schema v1 expected, header says v2
Poison-message retry loop begins, partition blocked
consumer_lag begins climbing; request_rate collapses toward 0.4 req/s

recommended_actions.action: Roll back order-service dep-6010 to the previous version (or restore the qty field / v1 header) to stop producing v2 events the consumer cannot parse.
recommended_actions.rationale: The producer schema change is the origin of the fault; reverting halts new malformed events.

recommended_actions.action: Ship a v2-compatible OrderExecuted deserializer (accept 'quantity'/v2) in settlement-service, then reset the poisoned consumer offset or move message orders-3@8841207 to a DLQ to unblock the partition.
recommended_actions.rationale: Unblocks the poison message and drains the 61k backlog once the schema is understood.

recommended_actions.action: Add producer/consumer schema-compatibility checks (contract tests / schema registry) to the order-service release pipeline before future OrderExecuted changes.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents a producer field rename from silently breaking downstream consumers.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on consumer_lag and poison-message retry loops with offset-level detail, and add a DLQ policy for undeserializable events.
recommended_actions.rationale: Lag took ~40 min to be noticed and the poison offset blocked all partitions.

data_gaps: No explicit metric for order-service event schema version or per-partition lag; partition-blocking inferred from log text.
Settlement-service logs sampled only partition orders-3; whether all partitions are blocked is inferred, not directly observed.
No consumer-group / offset-commit metrics to confirm the exact reset point needed for remediation.

findings.statement: order-service was deployed to v2.16.0 (dep-6010) at 07:40:00Z, renaming the OrderExecuted field 'qty' -> 'quantity' and bumping the event schema header to v2.

refs.quote: OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity

findings.statement: settlement-service logs show repeated deserialization failures on OrderExecuted events, first at 07:42:14Z, stating the consumer expects schema v1 but the header says v2.

refs.quote: failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)

findings.statement: settlement-service logs show poison-message retry loops blocking the partition on the same offset, with attempt counters in the tens of thousands (e.g. attempt 92490).

refs.quote: poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 92490), partition blocked

findings.statement: settlement-service consumer_lag rose from ~47 messages at 07:00-07:24 to 61,605 by 09:48, growing ~5000 per 12-min bucket.
settlement-service request_rate collapsed from ~62 req/s to 0.4 req/s in the 07:36-07:48 window and stayed at 0.4 through 09:48.
settlement-service CPU rose from ~28% to ~70% at the 07:36 bucket, consistent with a tight retry loop.
The config change cfg-3004 (consumer.max.poll.records 500->200) was applied at 07:35:37Z, and the settlement-service log line records it as applied.
There were zero settlement-service deployments in the window.
settlement-service restarts metric is 0 for every bucket, ruling out a restart/rebalance loop.
settlement-service db_pool_in_use stayed flat at ~6 connections throughout, ruling out DB pool exhaustion.
Kafka logs show only two benign idempotent-retry connection resets (07:27 and 09:51), no broker failure or rebalance storm.

refs.quote: retrying idempotent request (attempt 2) after connection reset

findings.statement: settlement-service HTTP error_rate stayed flat at ~0.2% (max 0.32) throughout, so the failure is in the consumer path, not HTTP serving.

Historical incident HIST-112 (settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment, categorized infrastructure_failure) is a superficially similar lead, but its signature (reassignment/rebalance) is not present here.

findings.statement: First deserialize error (07:42:14Z) follows the order-service deploy (07:40:00Z rollout complete 07:40:01Z) and the config change (07:35:37Z); the error onset aligns with the deploy, but the config change only reduced poll batch size and cannot cause a schema mismatch.
